subject: biology
pass: wave4 expert pass (Sonnet-equivalent CUET expert review, same procedure as waves 2 and 3)
reviewer_model: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (single reviewer, no other model run)
method: Every accepted biology question was solved by the reviewer from the stem, options and passage alone, then the key, explanation, options (longest-option giveaway, listed-order sequence keys, grammatical cues, option-set shape for match, sequence and statement items), unit and chapter against data/nta_blueprints/biology.json, the NCERT Class 12 Biology section (current 13-chapter numbering), the official CUET (UG) 2026 Biology syllabus PDF (data/CUET 2026/biology.pdf, units VI to X), the CUET level and time (72 s per question, no calculator) and the engine content gates were checked. The two passage sets were read as sets (passage word count, one chapter per set, 4 and 5 questions). The judge difficulty checks and notes in wave4-score-entries-2026-10-17.json were read after the independent solve and used to calibrate labels only.
scope: the 55 biology rows of docs/brain/reports/authored-w4/wave4-candidates-scored-2026-10-17.json (accepted by the rule), in file order: 46 standalone questions and two passage sets (w4-bio-02-set-1 with 4 questions, w4-bio-03-set-1 with 5 questions).
notes: No drops. All 55 questions sit in the CUET UG 2026 Biology syllabus (data/CUET 2026/biology.pdf, units VI to X): each stem maps to a named line, for example Unit X Biodiversity and Conservation lists 'narrowly utilitarian, broadly utilitarian and ethical' (Q55) and Unit IX lists 'molecular diagnosis' (the ELISA and probe set). Unit and chapter labels match data/nta_blueprints/biology.json for all 55; no excluded chapter (Reproduction in Organisms, Environmental Issues) is used.

Every key was re-derived independently and is correct and unique; no solver-visible text was changed (stems, options and passages are as accepted), so no blind re-solve is needed for these repairs. The 23 repairs touch only difficulty_label (7), ncert_ref (18) and explanation (3), with some questions carrying more than one.

difficulty_label (7): 5 hard to medium (f9edc91a, 89ff99c8, d8c5c153, ad0c0f11, cf3ce18f: single NCERT facts, linked NCERT lines or four recall statements; both quality judges' difficulty checks said medium for four of them, the fifth was split hard and medium), 1 medium to easy (ccbe9308, Trichoderma recall, both judges easy), 1 easy to medium (c4a7ad38, classifying a conservation argument, both judges medium). After this the pool is easy 17, medium 37, hard 1 against a blueprint target of 35, 50 and 15 percent; the only hard item left is 83d1ddf7 (anticodon from a template strand). The engine will have to fill the hard share from other waves or fall back to medium.

ncert_ref (18): chapter numbers 11, 13, 14 and 15 in the references were the unrationalised-book numbers for some chapters and wrong for the book the other references (Ch 7, 8, 9) use. Corrected to the current 13-chapter NCERT Class 12 Biology: Biotechnology and its Applications is Ch 10, Organisms and Populations Ch 11, Ecosystem Ch 12, Biodiversity and Conservation Ch 13. Section titles were not changed. This is from knowledge of the rationalised table of contents and was not checked against a copy of the book.

explanation (3): d157c263 (about 200 bp is the NCERT figure for a nucleosome, not the DNA wound round the octamer core), c2cb9280 (loose because-clause about the single-stranded probe), dc0f5ddb (unsupported 'common belief' remark). Stems, options and keys unchanged.

Passage sets: w4-bio-02-set-1 (cancer case, 4 questions, about 190 words) and w4-bio-03-set-1 (ELISA, PCR and probe case, 5 questions, about 230 words) are within the blueprint passage size (120 to 300 words), one chapter per set, 4 or 5 questions, every question answerable from the passage plus NCERT. Items 80acdc79, 53f7ec15 and 65134122 are easy partly because the passage states the cue; accepted as passage-reading items.

Left as is, noted: key position is balanced (A 14, B 13, C 14, D 14); longest-option checks show no giveaway (largest ratio 1.22 for 97c20f8d, 1.10 to 1.11 for 914f319b and c4e0c49c); 302af2c0 statement D (LH and FSH increase gradually in the follicular phase) is a direct NCERT line although one judge called it loose; b9de7d62 option says 'of menstruation' where NCERT says 'of the cycle' (same days 1 to 5); 83d1ddf7 needs the 3'/5' anticodon polarity, which is beyond the plainest NCERT wording but fair for the hard slot; a790d203 treats tRNA charging as step one, which is the NCERT order. No overlap with the wave 2 biology questions on a stem and option word-overlap screen.

Engine content gates (answer integrity, quality gate, structure, wording, corrupted wording, listed-order key) were re-run offline on the 55 rows with the repairs applied (scripts/authored-w4-engine-precheck.mjs on a patched copy kept outside the repo): 55 clean, 0 veto reasons.

verdicts.why: Vallisneria (and Hydrilla) is the NCERT water-pollinated plant; water hyacinth and water lily flowers rise above the water and use insects or wind, maize is a wind-pollinated grass. Key C is unique. Direct recall, easy.

Zygote, proembryo, globular, heart-shaped, mature embryo is the NCERT dicot order, so C, D, A, B (key A) is the only valid sequence; the other options each break the globular-before-heart rule or put the mature embryo early. Key is not the listed order. Medium.

Seed coat (integuments) and pericarp (ovary wall) are maternal tissue; embryo and endosperm come from fertilisation. Key D is unique (the embryo-seed coat slip is distractor B). Options are of equal length. Medium is right.

Testis, rete testis, vasa efferentia, epididymis, vas deferens, ejaculatory duct, urethra: C, A, D, B (key B). One blind solver of five picked the epididymis before the vasa efferentia, a slip not an ambiguity. Easy.

A is true (corpus luteum degenerates, endometrium breaks down, menstruation), D is true (NCERT: LH and FSH secretion increases gradually in the follicular phase, then peaks mid-cycle), B false (ovulation is mid-cycle, ends the follicular phase), C false. Key D (Only A and D) is unique. About 91 s, medium.

Secondary oocyte is arrested at metaphase II and completes meiosis II only when a sperm enters; key A is unique (B is the meiosis I step, C and D are the primary-oocyte stages). Correct and a standard board item, but both quality judges rated it medium and it is a single NCERT fact, so the label hard is too high.
verdicts.repair: difficulty_label hard -> medium. Solver-visible text unchanged.

verdicts.why: Trophoblast attaches to the endometrium, inner cell mass forms the embryo (NCERT). Key C is unique; the other rows each swap one role. Options of similar length. Medium.

Amniocentesis-IV, MTP-II, IUI-III, ZIFT-I (key A) match the NCERT definitions (ZIFT: zygote or early embryo up to 8 blastomeres into the fallopian tube). Options are real pairings, none is the listed order, A to D and I to IV are defined in the stem. Medium.

NCERT: pills are started preferably within the first five days of the menstrual cycle and taken for 21 days; key C is unique and A, B, D would be too late. The option says 'of menstruation' where NCERT says 'of the cycle', which is the same days 1 to 5 and not ambiguous. Left as is. Easy.
A is false (glutamic acid is replaced by valine, not the reverse), B, C and D are true NCERT statements, so B, C and D only (key B) is unique. Medium, four recall statements.
One gene (phenylalanine hydroxylase) causing mental retardation and reduced pigmentation is pleiotropy, the NCERT example. Key D is unique. Direct recall; the stem is only mildly signposted. Easy.
Queen has 32 chromosomes, the drone from an unfertilised egg is haploid with 16 and makes sperms by mitosis, so 16 and 16 (key B); 16 and 8 is the meiosis slip. NCERT haplodiploidy. Medium.

tRNA charging, ribosome binding at AUG, elongation, release factor at the stop codon: B, D, A, C (key C). Elongation cannot precede initiation and the release factor comes last. Charging first is the NCERT order of translation. Medium.

Histones are basic and rich in lysine and arginine (NCERT); key A is unique. The explanation said about 200 bp 'wind around each octamer' (the core wraps about 146 bp; 200 bp is the NCERT figure for a typical nucleosome including linker), reworded to the NCERT wording. Stem, options and key unchanged.
verdicts.repair: explanation reworded. Solver-visible text unchanged.

fields.explanation: Histones are positively charged basic proteins because they are rich in the basic amino acids lysine and arginine. This lets the octamer bind the negatively charged phosphate backbone of DNA, and a typical nucleosome contains about 200 base pairs of DNA helix. Aspartic and glutamic acids are acidic and would repel the DNA.

verdicts.why: 35S labels the protein coat, which stays outside the bacteria and is found in the supernatant after blending and centrifugation; key D is unique. Options are of equal length. Medium.

Template 3'-TACGGATCC-5' gives mRNA 5'-AUGCCUAGG-3'; third codon AGG; the antiparallel anticodon is 3'-UCC-5' (key C). 3'-GGA-5' is the anticodon of codon two, 3'-AGG-5' copies the codon. Unique, all four options same length. Hard is the right label (both judges), within CUET reach with NCERT's codon-anticodon pairing.
Miller's mixture was methane, ammonia, hydrogen and water vapour with no free oxygen; key D is unique. Easy.

Both extremes favoured and the mean disfavoured is disruptive selection: two peaks (key A); stabilising gives one narrower peak, directional shifts one peak. Key A is slightly the longest (48 against 37 to 43) but not a giveaway. Medium.
Typhoid is confirmed by the Widal test (NCERT); ELISA (HIV), biopsy (cancer) and PCR are the other NCERT tests. Key C is unique. Easy.
Allergy: IgE antibodies and histamine release from mast cells (NCERT); IgA is the colostrum antibody and macrophages are phagocytes. Key A is unique, options equal in length. Medium.
NCERT order: HIV enters a macrophage, RNA copied to DNA by reverse transcriptase, viral DNA integrates into host DNA, progeny viruses attack helper T cells: D, B, C, A (key D). Medium.
Heroin (diacetylmorphine) is made by acetylation of morphine from Papaver somniferum and is a depressant (NCERT). Key B is unique, the other rows change the drug, plant or effect. Medium.
